children: in a shift away from pursuing market share... Shally Seth Mohile Mumbai: Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India (HMSI) is prioritising dealer profitability and customer retention over pushing market share in the country's fiercely competitive two-wheeler market, with greater focus on expanding its vehicles in operation than chasing annual volume rankings. "Share is just one year's result.

Our business is not just one year," HMSI president and chief executive Tsutsumu Otani told ET. HMSI has been the country's second-largest two-wheeler maker since its separation from Hero MotoCorp in 2014, and even outsold its former partner in monthly sales on multiple occasions. During April-October FY27, HMSI's domestic dispatches stood at 3.7 million units, while Hero MotoCorp dispatched 4.0 million units.

Otani said HMSI will focus on growing and maintaining its units in operation (UIO), or the number of Honda vehicles on Indian roads. "For the dealer network, the most important thing is units in operation, not share," he said. "Honda tries to maintain units in operation. That means maintaining and protecting our dealer network, profitability and business." The strategy marks a shift in emphasis from the pursuit of market leadership to building a sustainable customer base in a market where competition has intensified across commuter motorcycles, scooters and premium bikes.

The focus on customer retention and repeat purchases comes as HMSI looks to tap growth across segments. The company sees considerable headroom in the motorcycle market, which Otani estimates at 23-24 million units annually. He also sees greater participation of women in personal mobility as an opportunity to expand the scooter market. Women currently account for only 10% of HMSI's business. A change in this mix could open up a new avenue of growth for the company, Otani said. HMSI registrations have been averaging 10-15% growth over the previous year, he said. The company expects sales during the September-November festive period to exceed 1.9 million units, compared with over 1.8 million units in the corresponding period last year.

title: HMSI to Focus on Dealer Margins, Buyer Retention
